item4_B3GEOMGAP.method: runB3GeomgapSweep(process.env, { counties: [...] }), one county per invocation (never batched), against PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL, read-only.

48491_Williamson_reverified.FLAG_VACUOUS_NOT_CONFIRMED: Sanity-checked this immediately because a clean 0 after a targeted fix is exactly the kind of result that deserves scrutiny, not celebration. Found: ALL 282,569 R-prefix cad_property accounts in Williamson (the only tax_year present, 2025) have land_value = NULL. The sweep's real-property predicate (land_acres > 0 AND land_value > 0) can therefore NEVER be satisfied by any R-prefix row in this county -- the R-prefix restriction itself is real and directionally correct (it does eliminate the numeric-roll-duality false-positive that produced >100,000 spurious 'orphans' before), but combined with the pre-existing land_value predicate, the measurement is now structurally BLIND for Williamson, not confirming a zero gap. This is a new finding, distinct from the already-known numeric-roll issue.

48209_Hays.note: Real, live-measured number; largest of the two now-confirmed-real counties. A null-saturated predicate can only UNDERCOUNT a true gap, never inflate it (both fields must be truthy to count), so this number is a safe lower bound even without independent sanity-checking. That sanity check (population size / null rate) was attempted but cut short by a fresh timeout before it returned (see contention) -- so it is not confirmed how close to complete this count is, only that it is not an overcount.

48309_McLennan.FLAG_VACUOUS_NOT_CONFIRMED: Same scrutiny applied. Found: land_acres is NULL for ALL 114,255 cad_property accounts in McLennan (the latest tax_year present) -- a DIFFERENT null pattern than Williamson (there it was land_value; here it is land_acres), but the same net effect: the real-property predicate can never fire. txgio_parcel has 130,650 rows for the county, so real geometry clearly exists; this is specifically an absence of land_acres in this county's cad_property ingestion, not a lack of underlying data. McLennan was never Williamson-special-cased, so this is a NEWLY discovered gap in the sweep's general predicate, not a repeat of the known Williamson quirk.

48453_Travis.note: Real, live-measured number (took longer than the earlier counties but completed cleanly, no timeout). item4_B3GEOMGAP.crossCuttingFinding: 2 of the 4 newly-attempted counties (Williamson, McLennan) produce a VACUOUS zero under the current land_acres > 0 AND land_value > 0 real-property predicate, for two different reasons (land_value null vs. land_acres null). doc-repo-bd rotated FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_REPLICA to a genuine direct host (verified independently: gcloud secrets versions list showed a real new version, and the runbook diff matched their description) and asked for a retry, flagging that a small replica compute -- not the query approach -- might be the real blocker.

Attempt 5: rewrote to avoid the join entirely (place_key already embeds county_fips as a text prefix per the migrations/0007 CHECK constraint, so a LIKE-prefix filter on parcel_record_cell alone needs no join to parcel_record) against the corrected replica. FAILED: same 57014 timeout -- ruling out the join as the cause.

Attempt 6: EXPLAIN (no ANALYZE, so it plans without executing -- costs nothing regardless of table size or contention) on attempt 5's query against the replica. Returned instantly: the planner already does the smart thing -- four Bitmap Index Scans on parcel_record_cell_pkey, one per county, each using the place_key range (e.g. >= '48209:' AND < '48209;') combined with rail_key='landUseCode', unioned via BitmapOr, then a 2-worker parallel Gather Merge and GroupAggregate. Estimated cost ~2.44M units against an estimated ~869,067 matching rows across the 4 counties.
item20_landUseFillMeasurement_factoryHal.conclusion: This is NOT a missing-index or bad-query-shape problem -- the plan was already optimal on the first well-designed attempt (attempt 5) and EXPLAIN confirms it. The timeout is genuine I/O/compute volume: ~869K rows to scan across 4 large counties, which the current replica compute apparently cannot get through inside a 45s bound. Reported this diagnosis back to doc-repo-bd, since it answers their own open question (their message speculated the replica compute might need resizing rather than the query being wrong) -- their hypothesis looks correct based on this EXPLAIN output, though only they/the operator can act on Neon compute sizing. Six real, independently-shaped attempts across two corrected endpoints is enough diligence for one night; stopping here rather than trying more variations of a query that's already provably well-planned.
